sections.h2: Where is Snohomish County and what drives its housing market?
sections.html:
Snohomish County lies north of Seattle on Puget Sound, with Everett as county seat and largest city. It is the third-most populous county in Washington, at 870,656 people in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, spread over about 2,087 square miles of land. The western side faces Puget Sound and holds most of the people, while the eastern side climbs into the Cascade Range and is largely national forest.

The county has 18 incorporated cities and two towns, Interstate 5 running through it, and the Tulalip Indian Reservation, created by the 1855 Point Elliott Treaty. Boeing began building its Everett assembly plant in 1967, and the Navy opened a homeport in Everett in 1994. Paine Field has had passenger service since March 2019. River valleys such as the Stillaguamish and Snohomish are farmed and occasionally flood during major weather events like atmospheric rivers.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 give a median owner-occupied home value of $696,000, a median household income of $111,246 and an owner-occupied rate of 68.2%. The mean commute is 30.8 minutes.

sections.h2: Which Snohomish County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor sets the value of taxable property, taxing district budgets and voter-approved measures determine the levy, and the Treasurer calculates and sends the bill. A separate Board of Equalization hears value appeals.

  • Assessor: main line 425-388-3433, residential appraisal 425-388-6555, commercial 425-388-3390, exemptions 425-388-3540.
  • Treasurer: 425-388-3366, with card payments by phone at 833-440-3332.
  • Board of Equalization: 425-388-3407, BOE@snoco.org, 3000 Rockefeller Ave m/s 409, Everett, WA 98201.

The county's assessment calendar shows when each step lands:

DateWhat happens
January 1Property is valued as of this date
February 15Property taxes can be paid on or after this date
April 30First-half taxes due; personal property listings due
July 1Board of Equalization petition deadline (depends on the mailing date of your notice)
July 15Board of Equalization meets in open session
October 31Second-half taxes due
November 30City and district budgets due to the County Legislative Authority

Source: Snohomish County, Important Assessment Dates.

sections.h2: When are Snohomish County property taxes due?
sections.html:
First-half or full-year Snohomish County tax is due April 30, and the second half is due October 31. Taxes under $50 for the year are due in full by April 30. The October 31, 2026 date has passed, so the next deadline is April 30, 2027.

By mail, a payment must be postmarked on or before the due date or the tax becomes delinquent. Online payments must be completed by the due date too. The Treasurer advises mailing several days early because of a change in the Postal Service postmark process, or asking a post office for a hand-stamped postmark or using certified mail. Allow 7 to 10 business days for a mailed payment to clear. A tax payment drop box on the county campus is open around the clock for checks; keep payments out of the ballot drop box.

The Treasurer's office has been moving to new software through summer 2026, and its page warns of delays on some requests, with electronic statements and account log-in unavailable at that time. If you need a payoff figure for a sale, call 425-388-3366 early.

sections.h2: What does late payment cost in Snohomish County?
sections.html:
If the first half is not paid by April 30, the full year's tax becomes delinquent, and interest or penalty is figured on the whole amount. Snohomish County assesses delinquent charges on the first day of each month.

The rate depends on the type of property. Under RCW 84.56.020, a home with four or fewer units, including a manufactured home, pays 9% annual interest and no penalty on taxes levied in 2023 or later. Other real property and personal property pay 12% interest, with a 3% penalty after June 1 and another 8% after December 1.

State law lets the treasurer waive interest and penalties when the county's own error kept a notice from reaching you, or when a spouse's death, or a parent's or stepparent's death, caused a missed payment on a personal residence and you notify the treasurer within 60 days (RCW 84.56.025). Payment agreements and partial payments are also allowed, with money going to the oldest year first.

sections.h2: How does the Snohomish County Assessor set a home's value?
sections.html:
The Assessor must value property at 100% of true and fair market value as of January 1. Snohomish County moved to annual revaluation with the 2004 assessment, so every property is appraised each year rather than in a four-year cycle. That means a falling market can lower values the next year and a rising one raises them.

Your tax is a share of what the taxing districts levy. The Assessor's value decides your share, while district budgets and voter-approved levies decide the total. Regular levies are limited to a 1% annual increase without a public vote. A value increase therefore does not always mean a tax increase of the same size.

Because assessments follow the calendar, sales in one year set the January 1 value of the next year and the taxes due the year after. This lag is built into the system and applies whether the market is rising or falling.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Snohomish County assessment?
sections.html:
File a petition with the Board of Equalization within 60 calendar days of the date on your Notice of Value, or by July 1 of the assessment year if no notice was sent, whichever is later. State law lets a county adopt a limit of up to 60 days, and Snohomish County has. There is no filing fee, and you submit a separate petition for each parcel.

The county's appeal guide lays out the steps:

  • Petition forms can be filed electronically on the county website until 4:00 PM on the deadline day, or on paper by mail or in person.
  • You receive a case number, and the Assessor reviews your petition. If you and the Assessor agree on a value, you sign a stipulation and the case closes.
  • If not, you get a hearing date about 60 days ahead. Hearings are held on Zoom, with in-person attendance possible if you tell the clerk at least a week before.
  • Evidence goes to both the board and the Assessor at least 21 business days before the hearing, up to 75 pages, with no audio, video or web links.
  • Decisions arrive by mail within 45 calendar days of the hearing.

The assessed value is presumed correct, so you carry the burden of clear, cogent and convincing evidence (RCW 84.40.0301). The board cannot use list prices, your ability to pay or the size of the increase. The best evidence is comparable sales near January 1, errors in square footage or other property records, and contractor bids for major repairs. Either side may appeal the board's decision to the State Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days of the mailing date. A decision affects only the assessment year appealed.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs apply in Snohomish County?
sections.html:
The Assessor runs a senior citizen and disabled person exemption, and the county page for 2024 lists a maximum disposable income of $75,000. Call 425-388-3540 or email assessor@snoco.org to learn the current limit, and use the county's status tool to follow an application.

Exempt participants are taxed on the lower of the frozen value from the date they qualified or the new market value. A state deferral program also exists for eligible seniors and disabled owners, and the tax statement must carry a notice describing both programs (RCW 84.56.020). Deferred tax becomes a lien on the property, and it must be repaid at transfer of ownership, which matters to any seller who deferred.

Open space and historic property programs carry their own dates. The county calendar sets October 1 as the last day to file for an exemption on historic property and December 31 as the open space application deadline.

sections.h2: What happens to Snohomish County tax when you sell?
sections.html:
Any tax still owed on a Snohomish County house must be paid out of the sale, so get a payoff for every unpaid year from the Treasurer before the closing date. Delinquent interest accrues from the first of each month, which makes a quote good only for the month it is issued.

The Department of Revenue says real estate excise tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and the seller usually pays. The state portion is graduated, and for sales from January 1, 2027 it starts at 1.1% on the first $551,000 and climbs in steps to 3.0% on any amount over $3,051,000. The local rate is added. Ask the Treasurer for the combined figure.

If delinquent tax sits for three years, RCW 84.64.050 requires the treasurer to issue certificates of delinquency and start foreclosure. A county cannot file a certificate when the delinquent tax is $100 or less. An income-qualified owner living in the home can have interest and penalties waived once foreclosure is under way (RCW 84.56.020).

faqs.q: When are Snohomish County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half or the full year, and October 31 for the second half. Taxes under $50 are due in full by April 30. The October 31, 2026 date has passed, and the next is April 30, 2027.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Snohomish County property value?
faqs.a: You have 60 calendar days from the date on your Notice of Value, or until July 1 of the assessment year, whichever is later. File with the Board of Equalization at 425-388-3407. There is no fee, and each parcel needs its own petition.

faqs.q: What is the interest on late Snohomish County property tax?
faqs.a: For a home with four or fewer units, interest is 9% a year with no penalty. Other property pays 12% a year, plus a 3% penalty after June 1 and 8% after December 1. If the first half is not paid by April 30, the full year becomes delinquent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Snohomish County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid from the proceeds at closing. Call the Treasurer at 425-388-3366 for a payoff for every year owed. Start early, since the office has warned about delays tied to a software change in summer 2026.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Snohomish County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay online through the Treasurer's payment site, by card over the phone at 833-440-3332, by mail, or in the campus drop box in Everett. Mail should be sent several days early, and mailed payments can take 7 to 10 business days to clear.
